## CroutonLayoutBreakpointAuthor

Breakpoints level of the Crouton Builder: author responsiveness by demonstration

File: `app/components/LayoutBreakpointAuthor.vue`

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `LayoutTree` | - | yes |  |
| `initialWidth` | `number` | - | no | Seed the ruler at a specific width instead of the viewport default — so a host that opens the author FROM a card of a known width (the builder's focus-edit / per-element-resize, #983) starts on that card's width, not 390/1280. Clamped to the ruler range. One-time seed (the author mounts fresh per edit); omit for the mobile-first-on-phone / desktop-first-on-wide default. |

## CroutonLayoutRenderer

Renders a layout data tree into resizable, nestable panes

File: `app/components/LayoutRenderer.vue`

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `LayoutNode` | - | yes |  |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Whether the splitter is draggable. `true` (default) is the authoring affordance — the editor / breakpoint-author / compose paths keep their resize handles. `false` is VIEW mode: a served layout renders at its breakpoint-resolved sizes with no draggable dividers (the end user doesn't redefine the layout). Stacking/min-width logic is unaffected either way — this gates only the handles. Threaded through the recursion. (#937) |

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `layoutChange` | `[node: LayoutSplit, sizes: number[]]` |
